argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only as a caveated form of launch readiness, not as a clean no-limitation certification. Aggregate readiness clears by 2.1 percentage points, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the launch configuration passed general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same admissible record also establishes that those completed checks do not cover post-visit instruction summarization, that this context is named in the deployment plan, and that its evals are not present in the packet. On that record, the supportable position is to preserve certification while narrowing the claim: certify overall release readiness, but do not represent the named post-visit summarization or telehealth discharge-planning context as evaluated, passed, or free of known limitations.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The admissible basis for avoiding escalation is that the remaining issue is a bounded overstatement risk in how certification is characterized, not a failure of aggregate launch-readiness evidence.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not require treating general readiness evidence as worthless; it permits general benchmarks and load tests to support launch readiness. But it also requires disclosure of material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts unless resolved or covered before clean certification. The admissible evidence therefore supports a caveated compliance posture: certification can be defended if the auditor evaluates the claim as limited to overall launch readiness and rejects any broader reading that would imply the named context already satisfies model-card coverage requirements. The current record does not support a clean finding that the named context has no known limitations.
concessions: The present packet does not contain admissible evidence of an incorporated certification artifact or model-card statement that already discloses the named evaluation gap.
The present packet does not contain admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance for launch with this named evaluation gap.

The present packet does not support any statement that post-visit instruction summarization or telehealth discharge-planning coverage has been evaluated, passed, or shown to have no known limitations.
